title: Polynomial substitution before desingularization quotients
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A a finitely presented R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], Lambda an R-algebra, pi in R and alpha:A→Lambda. Assume pi is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] in A and a compatible section A/pi^4 A→R/pi^4 R exists. Then there are n,m,c, a presentation P of A with c≤m, coefficients s_ik,r_ji, elements lambda_i of Lambda, and polynomials g_j,e_j in Q=R[v_1,...,v_c,w_1,...,w_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put xi_i=pi^2 sum_k s_ik v_k+pi^3 w_i and F_j=P.relation_j(xi). They satisfy: g_j=v_j+sum_i r_ji w_i+pi e_j; F_j=pi^3 g_j for j<c; F_j∈(pi^2) for every j; pi F_j∈(g)+(F)^2 for every j; alpha(P.val_i)=pi^4 lambda_i. No annihilator stability or smoothness conclusion is assumed.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Presentation. By (1) and the definition of strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] there are a presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], i.e. an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\theta:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ ($f_j\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]), and an integer $0\le c\le\min(n,m)$ such that (i) $\pi=\sum_{I\subset\{1,\dots,n\},|I|=c}a_I\,\theta\big(\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}\big)$ in $A$ for some $a_I\in A$ ($\partial/\partial x_i$ the formal partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]; $\theta(P)$ means $\theta$ of the class of $P$), and (ii) $\pi f_{c+j}\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)+(f_1,\dots,f_m)^2$ in $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ for $j=1,\dots,m-c$. Write $\rho$ for the map of (2) and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ for the given map; for $y\in A$ write $\bar y$ for its class in $A/\pi^4A$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1682-1691 (choice of the presentation and of c with (equation-strictly-standard-one) and (equation-star))

proof.text: Translation of the variables (Stacks: 'we can replace $x_i$ by $x_i-r_i$'). Choose $r_i\in R$ with $\rho(\overline{\theta(x_i)})=r_i\bmod\pi^4$ ($R/\pi^4R$ is a quotient of $R$). Let $\sigma$ be the $R$-algebra endomorphism of $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with $\sigma(x_i)=x_i+r_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; it is an automorphism with inverse $x_i\mapsto x_i-r_i$ (the composites fix every $x_i$, so are the identity by the uniqueness in the universal property). Put $f'_j=\sigma(f_j)$. Then $\sigma$ maps the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ onto $(f'_1,\dots,f'_m)$ and induces an isomorphism $\bar\sigma:R[x]/(f)\to R[x]/(f')$, so $\theta'=\theta\circ\bar\sigma^{-1}:R[x]/(f')\to A$ is again a presentation, with $\theta'(P)=\theta(\sigma^{-1}P)$, hence $\theta'(\sigma Q)=\theta(Q)$ for all $Q$, and $\theta'(x_i)=\theta(x_i)-r_i$, so $\rho(\overline{\theta'(x_i)})=0$. Derivatives: $\partial(\sigma Q)/\partial x_i=\sigma(\partial Q/\partial x_i)$ for all $Q$. Indeed $D_1=\partial_i\circ\sigma$ and $D_2=\sigma\circ\partial_i$ are $R$-linear and both satisfy $D(PQ)=\sigma(P)D(Q)+\sigma(Q)D(P)$ (Leibniz rule of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and multiplicativity of $\sigma$); $D_1(1)=D_2(1)=0$ and $D_1(x_k)=\partial(x_k+r_k)/\partial x_i=\delta_{ik}=\sigma(\delta_{ik})=D_2(x_k)$; by induction on the degree they agree on all monomials, hence everywhere by $R$-linearity. Therefore $\theta'\big(\det(\partial f'_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}\big)=\theta'\big(\sigma\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}\big)=\theta\big(\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}\big)$ ($\sigma$ is a ring map and the determinant a polynomial in the entries), so (i) holds for $(f',\theta')$ with the same $a_I$; applying $\sigma$ to a relation $\pi f_{c+j}=\sum_{k\le c}a_kf_k+\sum_{l\le l'}b_{ll'}f_lf_{l'}$ gives (ii) for $f'$. From now on we write $f_j,\theta$ for $f'_j,\theta'$ and $x_i$ also for $\theta(x_i)\in A$; thus $\rho(\bar x_i)=0$ for all $i$. Consequences: (a) $\rho\circ(A\to A/\pi^4A)$ is an $R$-algebra map $A\to R/\pi^4R$ killing every $x_i$, so it sends $\theta(P)$ to $P(0)\bmod\pi^4$ for every $P\in R[x]$ (both are $R$-algebra maps $R[x]\to R/\pi^4R$ agreeing on the $x_i$); applied to $\theta(f_j)=0$ this gives $f_j(0)\in\pi^4R$. (b) By the compatibility in (2), the class of $\alpha(x_i)$ in $\Lambda/\pi^4\Lambda$ is the image of $\rho(\bar x_i)=0$, so $\alpha(x_i)=\pi^4\lambda_i$ for some $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1692-1697 ('Say rho maps x_i to the class of r_i ... A -> Lambda maps x_i to pi^4 lambda_i')

proof.text: Linear terms and the unit $u$. Let $r_{ji}\in R$ be the coefficient of $x_i$ in $f_j$; write $f_j=f_j(0)+\sum_{i=1}^nr_{ji}x_i+Q_j$ with $Q_j$ a sum of monomials of degree $\ge2$, i.e. $Q_j\in(x_1,\dots,x_n)^2$. By the explicit formula of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] the constant term of $\partial f_j/\partial x_i$ is $r_{ji}$ (a monomial $rx^e$ contributes a constant only if $e$ is the $i$-th unit vector). Apply $\rho$ to (i): by Step 2(a), $\rho(\bar\pi)=\pi\bmod\pi^4$ and $\rho$ sends the image of $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j\le c,i\in I}$ to $\det(r_{ji})_{j\le c,i\in I}\bmod\pi^4$; choosing $r_I\in R$ with $\rho(\bar a_I)=r_I\bmod\pi^4$ we get $\pi=\sum_{|I|=c}r_I\det(r_{ji})_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}+\pi^4t$ for some $t\in R$. Put $u=1-\pi^3t\in1+\pi^3R$; then $u\pi=\sum_{|I|=c}r_I\det(r_{ji})_{j\le c,\,i\in I}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1697-1714 ('Write f_j = f_j(0) + sum r_ji x_i + h.o.t. ... for some u in 1 + pi^3 R')

proof.text: The matrix $(s_{ik})$. Let $M$ be the $n\times c$ matrix over $R$ with entries $M_{ij}=r_{ji}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $1\le j\le c$); $n\ge c$. For $I\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|I|=c$, the submatrix $M_I$ of the rows with index in $I$ is the transpose of $(r_{ji})_{j\le c,i\in I}$, so $\det M_I=\det(r_{ji})_{j\le c,i\in I}$ (a determinant equals that of its transpose). By Step 3, $u\pi$ lies in the ideal generated by the $c\times c$ minors of $M$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors](1) there is a $c\times n$ matrix $S'$ with $S'M=u\pi\cdot1_{c\times c}$. With $s_{ik}=S'_{ki}$ this reads $\sum_{i=1}^nr_{ji}s_{ik}=u\pi\,\delta_{jk}$ for all $j,k=1,\dots,c$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1715-1722 (Algebra, Lemma 07DQ, lemma-matrix-left-inverse)

proof.text: The elements $h_i$, $g_j$, $\varphi_j$. Let $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,v_1,\dots,v_c,w_1,\dots,w_n]$ and $\xi_i=\pi^2\sum_{k=1}^cs_{ik}v_k+\pi^3w_i\in R[v,w]$, $h_i=x_i-\xi_i\in P$. (a) Elimination: the $R$-algebra map $\epsilon:P\to R[v,w]$, $x_i\mapsto\xi_i$, $v\mapsto v$, $w\mapsto w$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], is surjective with kernel $(h_1,\dots,h_n)$: it kills the $h_i$, and $F-\epsilon(F)\in(h_1,\dots,h_n)$ for every $F\in P$ (true for $x_i$, $v_k$, $w_i$, and the set of such $F$ is closed under sums and products since $FG-\epsilon(F)\epsilon(G)=F(G-\epsilon G)+\epsilon(G)(F-\epsilon F)$); hence $P/(h)\cong R[v,w]$, and for every $F\in R[x]$, $F-F(\xi)\in(h)$. (b) Computation of $f_j(\xi)=\epsilon(f_j)$: since $\xi_i\in\pi^2R[v,w]$, $Q_j(\xi)\in(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n)^2\subset\pi^4R[v,w]$, and $f_j(0)\in\pi^4R$ (Step 2(a)); hence $f_j(\xi)\equiv\sum_ir_{ji}\xi_i=\pi^2\sum_{k=1}^c\big(\sum_ir_{ji}s_{ik}\big)v_k+\pi^3\sum_ir_{ji}w_i\pmod{\pi^4R[v,w]}$. For $j\le c$, Step 4 gives $\pi^2\sum_k(\sum_ir_{ji}s_{ik})v_k=u\pi^3v_j=\pi^3v_j+(u-1)\pi^3v_j$ with $(u-1)\pi^3\in\pi^6R$; so $f_j(\xi)=\pi^3\big(v_j+\sum_ir_{ji}w_i\big)+\pi^4e_j$ for some $e_j\in R[v,w]$. Put $g_j=v_j+\sum_{i=1}^nr_{ji}w_i+\pi e_j\in R[v,w]\subset P$ ($j=1,\dots,c$). Then $f_j(\xi)=\pi^3g_j$ in $R[v,w]$, $g_j\equiv v_j+\sum_ir_{ji}w_i\pmod\pi$, and by (a) $f_j-\pi^3g_j\in(h_1,\dots,h_n)$ in $P$. (c) For every $j$ (in particular $j>c$) each term of $f_j(0)+\sum_ir_{ji}\xi_i+Q_j(\xi)$ lies in $\pi^2R[v,w]$, so $f_j(\xi)=\pi^2\varphi_j$ for some $\varphi_j\in R[v,w]$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma 07CR (lemma-desingularize), lines 1723-1754 (the h_i, 'without further mention', the computation of f_j mod pi^4 and the choice of g_j)

proof.text: Apply the substitution to the strictly standard relation for every remaining equation. The first c equations are pi^3 times g_j, so their ideal is contained in G=(g). Hence pi F_j is in G+(F)^2 for every j. All F_j belong to (pi^2) by the explicit expansion. Rename the variables using ULift, which changes no polynomial identities. The chosen lift P.σ(algebraMap R A pi) and C pi have the same image in A, so their difference belongs to the relation ideal. Multiplying their difference by any relation belongs to its square; this justifies replacing the chosen lift by C pi before substitution.

proof_origin.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)
